interpretation: The recorded run failed because the measured minimum clearance was about 0.003 m, below the 0.05 m requirement by about 0.047 m. The same evidence shows the carriage stopped fully, had zero recorded wall-contact episodes, and settled within the allowed time. So the physical requirement that failed was minimum clearance, not final speed, contact count, or settling time. A supported parameter change to investigate is reducing speed_mps from 1.2 m/s, because the inspected analysis explicitly notes that ideal braking distance increases with speed squared and decreases with force; lowering initial speed is therefore directionally consistent with increasing retained clearance. This is only a proposal for future testing, not a verified fix.
hypotheses: The braking maneuver in this recorded case left too little residual distance to the wall even though no wall contact was recorded.
